gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the '4K rear' on two dual-4K cameras with the same IMX678 sensor is not recorded the same way: DashCamTalk's spec tables give the VIOFO A229 Ultra's rear camera 35 Mbps against 24 Mbps for the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K (front 36 vs 32 Mbps), all at 30 fps.
standout_why: I read both Product Bible pages that ChatGPT used. Best 4K Dash Cams (cited in chat 2) and Best Front and Rear Dash Cams (cited in chat 1) both give the A229 Ultra as 4K 30fps + 4K 30fps on IMX678 sensors. Neither gives a bitrate for any channel, and neither names the Vantrue S1 Pro Max, the 70mai A900 Ultra or the Rexing R88. The only other dual-4K model either page names is the BlackVue Elite 10 2CH. Both Car and Driver URLs refused the fetch and the VIOFO collection page returned HTTP 429, so I can't say what those three pages state. ChatGPT's own table calls every rear camera simply '4K', so no answer the shopper saw compares rear bitrate.
decides: This supports the A229 Ultra as the image-quality pick. On DashCamTalk's tables its rear camera gets about 46% more bitrate than the S1 Pro Max's (35/24 = 1.46), on the same IMX678 sensor at the same 30 fps, so it should keep more detail in plates and motion at night. Caveat: that A229 Ultra figure is from the page for the 3-channel kit; I could not open the 2CH listing. The Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K still belongs on the page as the lower-priced true dual-4K option on the question's own terms. Partner read supplied in the brief: $239.99 on 2026-11-21, against $299.99 for the A229 Ultra 2CH on Amazon in Product Bible's 2026-11-19 table; I could not read either price today. The footnote: both are '4K front + 4K rear', but the Vantrue writes its rear at 24 Mbps and DashCamTalk's table lists no rear HDR. The Vantrue does not yet have a Dealectric record, so it needs a new one (awin:vantrue, variant 51200752189749).
